sections.heading: Olympiad Circle Geometry, Power of a Point & Radical Axes Practice Exercises

questions.q: In the circle shown, chords \( AB \) and \( CD \) intersect internally at point \( P \). Given \( PA = 4 \), \( PB = 9 \), and \( PC = 3 \), find the exact segment length \( PD \).
questions.answer: By the Intersecting Chords Theorem (Power of a Point inside a circle), \( PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD \). Substituting gives \( 4 \cdot 9 = 3 \cdot PD \implies PD = \frac{36}{3} = 12 \).

questions.q: Cyclic quadrilateral \( ABCD \) (shown schematically) has consecutive side lengths \( AB = 3,\; BC = 4,\; CD = 3,\; DA = 4 \), and diagonal \( AC = 5 \). By Ptolemy's Theorem, find the exact length of the other diagonal \( BD \).
questions.answer: By Ptolemy's Theorem on cyclic quadrilateral \( ABCD \), the product of the diagonals equals the sum of products of opposite sides: \[ AC \cdot BD = AB \cdot CD + BC \cdot DA = 3(3) + 4(4) = 25. \] Dividing by \( AC = 5 \) gives \( BD = 5 \).

questions.q: In the Cartesian plane, circle \( \omega_1 \) has equation \( x^2 + y^2 = 33 \) and circle \( \omega_2 \) has equation \( (x - 4)^2 + y^2 = 33 \). Their radical axis (the locus of points having equal power with respect to \( \omega_1 \) and \( \omega_2 \)) is the vertical line \( x = x_0 \). Find \( x_0 \).
questions.answer: Equating powers \( (x^2 + y^2 - 33) = ((x - 4)^2 + y^2 - 33) \) cancels \( x^2 + y^2 \) and leaves \[ 8x - 16 = 0 \implies 8x = 16 \implies x_0 = 2. \]

questions.q: From an external point \( P \) to circle \( (O) \) shown, \( PT \) is tangent to the circle at \( T \) and a secant line through \( P \) intersects the circle at \( A \) and \( B \) (with \( A \) between \( P \) and \( B \)). If \( PA = 4 \) and the internal chord has length \( AB = 5 \), find \( PT \).
questions.answer: First compute the full secant length \( PB = PA + AB = 4 + 5 = 9 \) (a classic trap is multiplying \( PA \cdot AB \) instead of \( PA \cdot PB \)). By the Tangent-Secant Theorem, \( PT^2 = PA \cdot PB = 4 \cdot 9 = 36 \), so \( PT = 6 \).
